+    "addiction_liability": "Moderate to high abuse potential with significant risk of psychological dependence. The short duration of effects promotes bingeing, and compulsive redosing is commonly reported. Daily use patterns are not uncommon among those with regular access, making ketamine more psychologically compelling than most other psychedelics.",
+    "dependence_liability": "Physical dependence can develop with chronic use. Withdrawal symptoms include anxiety, tremor, sweating, and palpitations following cessation attempts.",

+      "ld50": "400 mg/kg (mice, IV); estimated human lethal dose approximately 200 mg/kg. Fatal blood concentrations typically range from 3-20 mg/L.",
+      "organ_toxicity": "Chronic use causes severe bladder damage (ketamine-induced ulcerative cystitis) in 20-30% of frequent users, including reduced bladder capacity to as low as 10-150 mL, urinary incontinence, painful urination, and blood in urine. Severe cases may require surgical bladder removal. Liver toxicity occurs in approximately 10% of heavy users. Kidney damage including acute kidney injury has been documented.",
+      "carcinogenicity": "Carcinogenicity studies have not been performed. Ketamine was shown to be clastogenic in mutagenesis studies.",
+      "other": "Neurotoxicity demonstrated in primate studies, with cell death in the prefrontal cortex after six months of daily use at recreational doses. Brain damage including reduction in both white and grey matter observed on MRI imaging in heavy users. Increased neuronal apoptosis in developing brains with prolonged exposure. Cognitive deficits including impaired verbal, short-term, and visual memory reported in frequent users."

+      "psychosis": "At anesthetic doses, 10-20% of adults experience emergence delirium with hallucinations and dysphoria. Chronic use may lead to persistent psychosis, paranoia, and delusional thinking. Increased dissociation and delusions observed in frequent recreational users even after abstinence.",
+      "self_harm": "Loss of pain sensation and motor control significantly increases injury risk. Multiple drowning deaths documented from unsupervised use near water or in bathtubs. Traffic accidents and suicides also implicated in ketamine-related fatalities.",
+      "seizure": "Seizures rare but reported at very high doses or overdose.",
+      "other": [
+        "Aspiration risk from vomiting while unconscious",
+        "Positional asphyxia from rapid loss of consciousness and suppressed pain response",
+        "Date rape facilitation due to confusion and amnesia effects",
+        "Respiratory depression including brief apneic episodes, especially with rapid IV injection",
+        "Contraindicated in severe cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled psychosis, increased intracranial pressure, severe liver disease, and pregnancy"
+      ]

# Dextromethorphan · #282

+    "addiction_liability": "Moderate abuse potential with documented cases of psychological addiction. Regular use can lead to emotional dependence and craving; some users report daily use patterns that are difficult to discontinue.",
+    "dependence_liability": "Physical dependence develops with chronic use. Withdrawal symptoms include fatigue, apathy, flashbacks, constipation, insomnia, nightmares, anhedonia, memory impairment, attention deficits, and decreased libido. Symptoms resemble antidepressant discontinuation syndrome due to DXM's serotonin reuptake inhibition.",
-      "ld50": "",
-      "organ_toxicity": "",
+      "ld50": "No formal LD50 established. Lethal doses estimated at 2,200 mg or greater, though fatalities are rare and typically involve co-ingredients or polydrug use.",
+      "organ_toxicity": "Overdose may cause rhabdomyolysis leading to kidney damage, cardiac complications including severely elevated heart rate and blood pressure, and urinary retention. Multi-ingredient formulations containing acetaminophen pose significant hepatotoxicity risk at recreational DXM doses.",
-      "other": ""
+      "other": "Potential neurotoxicity with heavy chronic use. While oral DXM did not produce Olney's lesions in rat studies, adolescent administration impaired learning in adulthood. Chronic users report persistent deficits in memory, attention, abstract language comprehension, and visual processing that may persist for months after cessation."
-      "psychosis": "",
-      "self_harm": "",
-      "seizure": "",
-      "other": []
+      "psychosis": "Large doses and extended use (3+ consecutive days of heavy use) associated with psychotic breaks and toxic psychosis. Lasting delusional, paranoid, or psychotic ideation may persist for days to months. High plateau experiences commonly produce paranoid ideation, delusions of persecution, and perceived contact with entities.",
+      "self_harm": "Risk of accidental injury due to anesthetic effects, ataxia, and loss of motor control. High doses may produce inappropriate or violent behavior in response to hallucinations and delusions.",
+      "seizure": "Seizures reported at high doses and during overdose. Fever combined with seizures can lead to brain cell death.",
+      "other": [
+        "Respiratory depression is a rare but serious side effect at high doses",
+        "Hyperthermia may occur at overdose levels",
+        "Multi-ingredient cough/cold products containing acetaminophen, chlorpheniramine, or doxylamine pose severe risk of organ damage or death when consumed at recreational DXM doses",
+        "Adolescents and individuals with psychiatric disorders are at elevated risk of problematic use"
+      ]
